title: What does AMMBid do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AMMBid and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AMMBid spends liquidity-provider tokens to bid for an AMM's discounted trading-fee auction slot. [1]

The auction slot offers a temporary trading-fee advantage rather than ownership of the pool or a guaranteed return. Bid bounds and authorized accounts control who may use the benefit. Compare the LP tokens consumed with the expected fee saving. A winning bid does not protect against price movement or eliminate every trading cost. [1]

The AMMBid reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using AMMBid, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
